author: Rahul kp
title: Compound Interest
simple_words: Each period, interest is added to the principal, so the next interest is earned on a bigger amount.

definitions.meaning: Interest calculated on principal plus interest already added in earlier periods. CI = Amount − Principal.
The equivalent annual rate, compounded once a year, that gives the same final amount as the nominal rate compounded m times a year.

key_points: For the same rate and time, CI is more than simple interest when time is above one period.
==Nominal rate== is the stated yearly rate; ==effective rate== shows the true yearly growth.
More compounding periods in a year means a higher effective rate.
!!If compounding is yearly, effective rate equals nominal rate.!!

formulas.name: Amount with compounding
formulas.legend: A = amount, P = principal, r = nominal annual rate in %, n = years, m = compounding periods per year

formulas.name: Compound interest
formulas.legend: CI = compound interest, A = final amount, P = principal

formulas.name: Effective annual rate
formulas.legend: E = effective rate (decimal), i = nominal annual rate (decimal, 8% = 0.08), m = periods per year

insight.text: Compounding more often within a year raises the effective rate above the nominal rate.

trick_hook: divide the rate, multiply the time

memory_trick.explanation: Compounding m times a year: divide the annual rate by m and multiply years by m. Half-yearly: half the rate, double the periods.

steps: Convert rate to r/m per period
Convert time to m × n periods
Subtract P if CI is asked
exam_tip: Read the words "per annum, compounded half-yearly" first; options often include the yearly-compounding answer as a trap.

doubt.question: Is the effective rate always higher than nominal?
doubt.answer: Only when compounding is more than once a year. With yearly compounding, both are equal.

mistakes.wrong: Reporting A as the compound interest
mistakes.right: CI = A − P. Subtract the principal at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Using full annual rate for half-yearly compounding
mistakes.right: Use r/2 per period and 2n periods.

mistakes.wrong: Putting r = 8 inside the effective rate formula
mistakes.right: Use i = 0.08 in decimal, then E = (1 + i/m)^m − 1.

mistakes.wrong: Using time in years with a per-period rate
mistakes.right: Rate and time must be in the same period unit.

check_notes: Checker 1: Steps 2 and 4: step 2 gives the per-period rate as r/m, and step 4 writes A = P(1 + rate)^periods. Formula 1, however, defines r as a percentage (e.g. 8). Read literally, the steps could give 1 + 4 instead of 1 + 0.04. Correct version: 'Convert the rate to r/(100m) per period (as a decimal)' and 'A = P(1 + r/(100m))^(mn)'. This brings the steps in line with formula 1 and mistake 3.
